title: DELETE Statement vs TRUNCATE
description: Remove rows safely, compare DELETE and TRUNCATE performance and locking, and understand WAL generation.

data.text: Deleting rows can be accomplished with either `DELETE` or `TRUNCATE`. While both remove records, their underlying database engine implementations and performance profiles are radically different.

rows: Marks each tuple as dead (requires VACUUM later)
Deallocates disk pages immediately; creates new empty file
High (logs deletion of every single row)
`ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` (locks entire table from all reads/writes)
Yes (can be rolled back in PostgreSQL!)

data.title: DELETE with USING Clause and RETURNING
data.content: Deleting records matching criteria in another table.
data.code:
DELETE FROM session_tokens st
USING expired_accounts ea
WHERE st.user_id = ea.user_id
RETURNING st.id, st.user_id;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `DELETE` when removing specific filtered rows.
Use `TRUNCATE` when emptying an entire table; it is hundreds of times faster.
In PostgreSQL, `TRUNCATE` is fully transaction-safe and can be rolled back.
